sources.claim: Indexed recurrent KDA honors token index strides, sizes separate output states per flattened token, and avoids state writes when state output is disabled. CUDA and Ascend paths are changed.
implementation_reading: CUDA initial/final index loads multiply i_t by stride_indices_tok.
Separate final_state allocation uses B*T instead of sequence count N when ssm_state_indices is supplied, protecting per-token storage bounds.
Continuous-batching writes additionally require STORE_FINAL_STATE, preserving a borrowed initial state pool when output is disabled.
Ascend uses corresponding per-token allocation and block-pointer boundary checks plus ascend_compile_kwargs; present-head Ascend runtime remains an author-disclosed gap.
sources.memory_implication: Correct storage can require MORE allocated memory (B*T state records rather than N). No lower-memory benefit is established; preserving aliased pools and correct state capacity precedes allocation optimization.
sources.tests_read: 48 parametrized indexed cases span dense/packed, state orientations, stride1/2, accepted token1/2, in-place/separate/disabled output; compare naive outputs/states, untouched pool slots, returned shapes and resumed decoding. Tests not executed locally.

sources.claim: Only default dense recurrent output allocation changes from zeros_like(v) to empty_like(v); packed allocation retains zeros_like(v), and caller-supplied out remains the same buffer.
implementation_reading: Single production-line conditional: empty_like(v) if cu_seqlens is None else zeros_like(v).
Caller-provided out validation/identity route is retained; no kernel arithmetic, launch geometry or state-allocation change in this diff.
sources.memory_implication: Removing dense initialization saves a write pass, not the output tensor bytes. Correctness requires complete writes of every dense output element; packed unused capacity still needs zeros and supplied-buffer suffix must retain its original contents. No GPU peak-memory reduction is shown.
